title: Sectionwise module comparison over an identity open and its underived coherence
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be any commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For every scheme $T$, on small representatives of $T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ in the common coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal M_T=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Use the specified module functors $f^*,f_*$ and coefficient comparisons from pullback from the point [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ and $j':U\hookrightarrow Z'$ be open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $h:Z'\to Z$ satisfy $hj'=j$ and $h^{-1}(j(U))=j'(U)$ as open subschemes.
For every $v:V\to U$ in $U_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, the projection $\pi_{h,V}:V\times_Z Z'\to V$ is an isomorphism with inverse $(1_V,j'v)$, natural in $V$. The functor $j^*$ on module objects is sectionwise restriction to the localized site: $(j^*M)(V)=M(V\to U\to Z)$, with $\Lambda_U$-action transported through the inverse of $\alpha_j:j^*_{\mathrm{Ab}}\Lambda_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_U$; the same assertion holds for $j'$. There is a unique natural module isomorphism $c_h:j^*h_*\xrightarrow{\sim}j'^*$ whose map at $M,V$ is $M(\pi_{h,V}^{-1}):M(V\times_Z Z')\to M(V)$ under these restriction identifications. Thus its section map is the identity after $\pi_{h,V}$; it is linear for the specified coefficient actions.
Let $j'':U\hookrightarrow Z''$ be an open immersion and $k:Z''\to Z'$ satisfy $kj''=j'$ and $k^{-1}(j'(U))=j''(U)$. Write $\mu_{h,k}:h_*k_*\xrightarrow{\sim}(hk)_*$ for the specified module compositor [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp]. Then
$$c_{hk}=c_k\circ(c_hk_*)\circ(j^*\mu_{h,k}^{-1}).$$
For $h=1_Z$ and $j'=j$, $c_h$ is the identity after the canonical sectionwise comparison $(1_Z)_*\cong1_{\mathcal M_Z}$. All equations include functor associators and the canonical fibre-product identifications. No derived category, properness, density, or field of definition is assumed.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib IsOpenImmersion.isPullback to the two open immersions and the inverse-image condition. This gives the cartesian square with vertices U,Z',U,Z and maps j',1_U,h,j. Its universal property implies that for P=V times_Z Z', the second projection is the first projection followed by v and j'. Therefore (1_V,j'v) is inverse to the first projection. Comparing the two projections proves naturality in V.

proof.text: Take beta from [lem-sfb-module-direct-image-open-pasting]. Its Sectionwise clause supplies bijectivity of all the specified open coprojections. The existing scalar-extension/comap-inverse comparison composed with the extension unit is identity on underlying sheaves (upperStarLowerStarAdjunction_homEquiv_hom and extendUnitHom_extendScalarsIsoComapInv_hom_app). Naturality along the graph arrow then proves exactly the displayed OpenRestriction action formula.

proof.text: Apply beta to the cartesian representative (j',1_U,h,j) directly, and compose with lowerStarId on U. This defines c_h without a replacement of the specified module functors. Sectionwise normalization of beta, naturality of coprojections in site objects, and the section formula for lowerStarId show that c_h is restriction along (1_V,j'v): composing the sectionArrow with the inverse identity-pullback projection has exactly these two projections.

For two normalized comparisons, use surjectivity of each source coprojection to reduce equality on any section to the normalization formulas. Apply extensionality successively for additive group maps, presheaf natural transformations, sheaf maps, module maps and natural isomorphisms.

proof.text: Check composition on a source coprojection. Naturality of coprojections in module maps moves upperStar of lowerStarComp inverse through that coprojection. Apply the two normalization formulas and the section formula for lowerStarComp inverse from the Composition clause of [lem-sfb-module-direct-image-open-pasting]. Sheaf functoriality combines the three resulting restrictions. The composite geometric arrow and the direct inverse (1_V,j''v) agree by their two pullback projections, using j''k=j'. Thus the module transformations agree by sectionwise extensionality. This proves the required associator and inverse-compositor order directly.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q101-a11ee2abc (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: a one-level split of lem-sfb-identity-open-module-sections into 6 steps, with no new nodes. There is no re-split note, the statement, stmt_deps and source are unchanged, and there is no SGA citation. The dependency closure is acyclic, including the nodes added by the fix. Sources checked: Stacks 0D6G (sites-cohomology l.4374), whose proof rests on 04J0 (sites-modules l.2369, f'_*j_U^{-1}=j_V^{-1}f_*); 04IX and 03D6 checked in tags/tags. Step 1: the inverse (1_V,j'v) and its naturality are correct, and the hypothesis h^{-1}(jU)=j'(U) is needed. Step 2: clause (1) of the slice localization holds with no constant-ring restriction; alpha is invertible for any condensed ring; change-of-scalars clause (5) gives Ext_alpha = Res_{alpha^{-1}}, with the right direction. Step 3 had a gap, now repaired: h_U=pi_{h,U}: Z'x_ZU->U is only an isomorphism, so applying the pasting lemma's identity-morphism normalization was not literal, and the transport from (h_U)_*j_S^* to j'^* had no citation. The step now states h_U s_U=1 and j_S s_U=j'. (h_U)_* is identified with s_U^* via lower-star-comp and the upper/lower adjunction, and s_U^*j_S^* with j'^* via upper-star-comp. The resulting c_h is a composite of module isomorphisms, so it is linear. proof_deps was recomputed. Step 4: uniqueness holds because a module morphism is its underlying sheaf morphism. Step 5: pasting clause (d) with f=k and g=h has types and order matching the item, and the explicit check of sections along (1_V,j''v) confirms it. Step 6: the identity case is correct. lem-sfb-module-direct-image-open-pasting is strictly more general than the item, so it is a specialization, not a duplicate. Accepted tool uses: weakly-etale localization, ringed open comparison, and the open-pasting lemma; none of them replaces the unit's compactification route. Small cases checked: U empty, h=id, U=Z, and nonconstant Lambda.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
